briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon, everyone. I will now begin the climate briefing for September 9, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Warning from the Frontline of the Climate Crisis: Deepening Global Impacts
sections.content: Today's news once again reminds us of the severe global impacts and vulnerabilities caused by climate change. Domestically, seaweed and aquaculture farms in the Jeju region are directly impacted by climate change, with warnings that this could lead to a crisis for local specialties like 'Momguk' [3, 6, 9]. The Earth is projected to experience a 25% greater warming effect than anticipated, even with the same greenhouse gas emissions [12], and in Vietnam, extreme weather events are becoming commonplace, with record climate highs being extensively broken due to August's heavy rainfall and heatwaves [36]. Internationally, Nepal is demanding climate justice and compensation following devastating floods, while the European Alps face glacier retreat and rockfall threats [131, 156, 160], and heavy rainfall from Hurricane Lowell in Hawaii is linked to rising Pacific ocean temperatures [136], indicating a global emergency.

sections.title: 🌍 International Voices for Climate Justice
sections.content: As the damage from climate change intensifies, international discussions regarding accountability are also becoming more active. Nepal has demanded over $20 million in compensation from the UN for damages caused by severe floods, emphasizing that major economic powers bear responsibility for climate change [16, 23, 26, 131, 158]. This is considered a significant move to amplify the call for 'climate justice' concerning the unequal impacts of climate change. Meanwhile, the UN is urging joint action to address air pollution and climate change [138], and the observation that many people still do not recognize the link between climate change and extreme weather events [133] highlights the need for improved awareness.

sections.title: 🌱 Expansion of Domestic Carbon Neutrality Practices and Adaptation Efforts
sections.content: Amidst this crisis, positive movements for climate change adaptation and carbon neutrality are expanding both domestically and internationally. Gunpo City received the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport Award in the climate change category of the '2026 Korea Urban Awards,' recognizing its climate response achievements [4, 11, 21, 31], and Pyeongtaek City was awarded the Presidential Award for its carbon neutrality efforts through the hydrogen industry [38, 39, 40]. Furthermore, the Climate Crisis Adaptation Act passed the National Assembly, establishing a risk assessment and support system for vulnerable groups [32], and the '10 Million Climate Citizens' campaign is encouraging public participation in carbon neutrality practices [42, 43, 44, 70]. Numerous local governments, including Seoul, Chungnam, and Gyeongnam, have been selected as outstanding municipalities for carbon neutrality implementation, leading region-specific green innovation [41, 58, 74, 77, 78, 83].

sections.title: 💡 Accelerating Renewable Energy Transition and Green Industry Cooperation
sections.content: The transition to renewable energy for achieving carbon neutrality goals is showing concrete results across various sectors. Jeju Energy Corporation was recognized as a national exemplary institution, receiving the Minister of Environment Commendation for its contributions to renewable energy safety management [85, 87, 103], and Jeju Samdasoo is actively implementing sustainable management by commencing product manufacturing and water source operations with eco-friendly renewable energy [96, 100, 109, 126, 129]. KB Financial Group and BS Group have agreed to strengthen strategic cooperation in renewable energy and AI data center sectors, expanding productive finance [86, 91, 92, 93, 95, 97, 98, 99, 104, 108, 112, 113, 116, 119, 120, 122, 128], and the government announced 648 billion KRW in financial support to achieve the 100GW renewable energy target [90]. Concurrently, green technology innovation is actively underway, with various safety technologies to prevent large-capacity battery fires being showcased at the 'K-Battery 2026' exhibition [130].

briefing.closing: Today's climate briefing highlights the severe impacts of climate change, alongside the simultaneous, multifaceted efforts and innovations underway both domestically and internationally to overcome them. Alongside international responsibility for the climate crisis, continuous transition efforts across local communities and industries will become even more crucial. This concludes today's climate briefing.
